questions.q: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
o: We have not received
our coast guards yet
some information from
questions.s:
Solution:

  • The sentence is:
    "We have not received some information from our coast guards yet."

  • The error lies in the phrase: "some information from"

  • Explanation:

  • When used in negative sentences, we typically use "any" instead of "some".

  • "Some" is generally used in affirmative sentences, while "any" fits naturally with negatives and questions.

  • Therefore, the correct phrase should be: "We have not received any information..."

  • Why the other options are correct:

  • "We have not received" – grammatically correct.

  • "our coast guards yet" – correctly placed and used.

  • "No error" – incorrect because an error exists in the sentence.

Corrected sentence:
"We have not received any information from our coast guards yet."

questions.q:
Lenovo has launched ThinkPad XI Fold, the world's first foldable laptop which is claimed to be so durable as its other devices.

[CHSL 12/10/20 S1]
questions.s: The correct structure for comparison is "as...as." Therefore, the sentence should read: "Lenovo has launched ThinkPad XI Fold, the world's first foldable laptop which is claimed to be as durable as its other devices.”

questions.q:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No Improvement'.

She is as good if not better than her sister.
questions.s:
The correct answer is as good as.

Key Points

  • When in the same sentence two adjectives in different degrees of comparison are used, both should be complete in themselves.
  • The phrase "not better than" may mean "worse" or "almost the same."
    • Example: Divya is as good as if not better than her brother. 
  • We use as + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons when the things we are comparing are equal in some way:
    • For Example - The world’s biggest bull is as big as a small elephant.
  • 'As good' should be replaced by 'as good as'.
  • Thus, the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence is option 2.


Correct Sentence: She is as good as if not better than her sister.

questions.q:
The money arrived when I (little) expected it.

[Phase-X (12TH LEVEL) 02/08/2022]
o: The money arrived when I least expected it.
The money arrived when I less expected it.
The money arrived when I expected it.
The money arrived when I little expected it.
questions.s: "Least" is the superlative form of "little" and is used to express the lowest degree of expectation in this sentence.

questions.q:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options.

Select the correct alternative.

The new almirah is big than this one.
questions.s:
The comparative form of "big" is "bigger," used here to compare two almirahs.

More big: Incorrect, as "bigger" is the standard form.

Biggest: Superlative, used for more than two items.

More bigger: Redundant and incorrect.

The correct sentence: The new almirah is bigger than this one.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a)

questions.q: We can discuss the details of the project latter during the meeting.
o: We can discuss the
details of the project
latter during the meeting.
questions.s:
The correct option is (c) "latter during the meeting."

In this context, "later" is used to refer to a subsequent time during the meeting, so "latter" is incorrect. "Later" is the correct term to indicate a future point in time.

The corrected sentence would be: "We can discuss the details of the project later during the meeting."

questions.q: This is (a) / a very good (b) / movie to watch. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'Very good' is correct for positive degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'very good' positive degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q: Radha climbed the / ladder cautious, / but she fell off / despite being careful.
questions.s:
Cautious” is an adjective, but here it is incorrectly used to describe how Radha climbed.
The sentence needs a describing word that correctly fits the action, and “cautious” cannot function in that position.
Correct form: Radha climbed the ladder cautiously…

questions.q: This is (a) / a very interesting (b) / story. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'Very interesting' is correct for positive degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'very interesting' positive degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q:
When I met the couple yesterday I noticed that the wife was more taller than her husband.

[CGL Mains- 28/01/2022]
questions.s: "More" is not used with comparative adjectives like "taller." The correct form is "the wife was taller than her husband."

questions.q:
A study finds that the average staff cost at/a public sector bank is high than that at/its private sector counterpart.

(SSC CHSL Tier-01 09/03/23)
o: A public sector bank is high than that at
A study finds that the average staff cost at
questions.s: "is high than" is incorrect. The correct form should be "is higher than" because "higher" is the correct comparative form of "high.”

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with a suitable adjective.

Anamika is the smartest and _____ of all students.
questions.s:
Two adjectives which refer to the same noun or pronoun joined by conjunction must be in the same degree of comparison. So, the blank will be filled by a superlative form of adjective. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The final sentence will be: Anamika is the smartest and kindest of all students.

questions.q:
He was enough tall / to be admitted / into the armed forces.

[CPO 10/11/2022 S3]
o: He was enough tall
questions.s: The correct phrase is "tall enough" (adjective + enough) instead of "enough tall.”

questions.q: The beautiful young girl (a) / jumped into the river (b) / in a state of depression. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Jumped to to the river' should be 'jumped into the river.' Answer: (b). 'Jumped to to the river' galat hai, sahi form hai 'jumped into the river.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: Jack has a far more larger apartment (a)/ and luxurious apartment (b)/ than John's. (c)/ No error (e)
o: Jack has a far more larger apartment
questions.s: Use "far larger and more luxurious apartment" instead of "far more larger.”

questions.q: "Can you give me so many examples of subordinate clauses?", the teacher asked the class.
questions.s: (b) Explanation:- Some ke sath many ya few ka use nhi hota opposite meaning hone ki wajah se. Sentence ke meaning ke according ' teacher yhan students ko aur examples ke liye puch rha hai' isliye 'some more examples' ka use hoga.

questions.q: His words became harsherly as the argument escalated.
questions.s:
Generally, verbs are modified by adverbs. But verbs of sensation (seem, look, appear, feel, taste, sound, and smell) and ‘be’, ‘become’, ‘turn’, ‘get’, ‘grow’, ‘keep’, ‘make’, and ‘prove’ are followed by an adjective and not an adverb.

The correct option is (b) "harsherly." So, the error lies in using "harsherly," which is not the correct adverb form. Instead, the correct form is "harsher."

The correct sentence should be: "His words became harsher as the argument escalated."

questions.q:
It turned out to be the noisy park party anybody had ever attended.

{ CGL Tier-02 08/08/22}
o: Anybody had ever attended
It turned out to be
The noisy park party
questions.s: The adjective "noisy" should be placed before the noun "party". Also, the word "anybody" should be in the correct form as "anyone" for better clarity and flow. The sentence structure needs to be modified to use the proper comparative form: "the most noisy" or "the noisiest".

questions.q: In the five next/years, the migration/will surely stop. (SSC CHSL Tier-01 09/03/23)
questions.s: The correct order for multiple adjectives is ordinal before cardinal: "the next five years".

questions.q: I have never seen a man / get off his horse quick as / did that stranger Englishman. (SSC MTS Tier-01 14/06/23)
o: get off his horse quick as
I have never seen a man
questions.s: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'get off'. The phrase should be "as quickly as".

questions.q: The children played in the three-acres field behind the house.
o: field behind the house
questions.s:
Many nouns are a part of compound adjectives or hyphenated. They never come in plural form.

The correct option is (b) "in the three-acres." So, the error lies in using "three-acres" instead of "three-acre" to match the singular noun "field." Additionally, "three-acre" should be hyphenated when used as a compound adjective.

The corrected sentence should be: "The children played in the three-acre field behind the house."

questions.q:
The wedding reception will be hosted in Mumbai at a late date.

[ CHSL 20/10/20S2]
o: at a late date
questions.s: "At a late date" should be changed to "at a later date". "Later" is used to indicate a future time, while "late" refers to something happening after the expected time.

questions.q: Your comment (a) / on this issue (b) / is more right (c) / and I am with you all along the way. (d) / No error (e)
o: and I am with you all along the way.
questions.s: Use "more correct" instead of "more right"
